holidays.name: National Cereal Day
holidays.description: Grab your biggest bowl and your favorite spoon. This day celebrates the crunchy, sugary, and sometimes wholesome staple of the American breakfast table. Whether you pour flakes, puffs, or marshmallow shapes, today is a good day to eat dessert-adjacent food before noon.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance. It honors cereal's rise to become one of America's most popular breakfast foods since the late 19th century.
holidays.funFact: Cereal began as a health food in the late 1800s. Early versions were meant to be bland and nutritious, which is a long way from today's marshmallow-studded bowls.

holidays.name: National Flapjack Day
holidays.description: Flapjacks are a good reason to stack your plate high. Pancakes are the star here. Today is for syrup, butter, and fluffy griddle goodness, and for flipping breakfast with confidence.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It gives pancake fans a second excuse to celebrate in the breakfast season.
holidays.funFact: "Flapjack" is an old name for pancake, and it has been used in English for centuries. In parts of the UK, a flapjack means a chewy oat bar instead.

holidays.name: National Crown Roast of Pork Day
holidays.description: This day honors a dramatic centerpiece. A crown roast of pork is a rack of ribs shaped into a circle, so it looks like a royal crown. It's a showstopping dish for dinner parties and holidays.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a classic, elegant roast.
holidays.funFact: Cooks often put paper frills on the exposed rib tips and fill the center of the crown with stuffing. This makes the roast look even fancier.
